harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 (OpenWrt) as the router for the shared private network 10.100.34.0/24 with node2/node3: gave it a fixed static address (kept its existing 10.100.34.10 to avoid breaking the exec transport), enabled its dnsmasq DHCP server to serve node2/node3 (required setting dhcp.lan.force='1' since dnsmasq initially detected and deferred to the platform's own DHCP server present on the same L2), and added a firewall rule rejecting TCP/23 from the lan zone. Verified all three settings live via actual traffic tests (nmap broadcast-dhcp-discover from node2/node3 showing node1 as a DHCPOFFER source; nc showing TCP 23 refused while TCP 22 still succeeds), both before and after restarting all three nodes one at a time, confirming a changed boot_id and full functional recovery on each node.
actions_performed: Inspected initial network state on node1 (OpenWrt 25.12.2, br-lan/eth0, proto=dhcp) and node2/node3 (Ubuntu 24.04, enp1s0, DHCP-leased from platform gateway 10.100.34.1)

Set node1 network.lan proto to static with ipaddr=10.100.34.10, netmask=255.255.255.0, gateway=10.100.34.1; committed and reloaded network (kept the existing address so the SSH-based exec transport to node1 was not disrupted)
Added firewall rule 'Block-Telnet-From-LAN' (src=lan, proto=tcp, dest_port=23, target=REJECT); committed and reloaded firewall

Discovered dnsmasq was refusing to start its DHCP server because it detected the platform's own DHCP server already active on br-lan; set dhcp.lan.force=1 and restarted dnsmasq so it actually serves leases in the configured 100-249 range
Started a socat TCP listener on port 23 on node1 (busybox nc lacks listen support) so the REJECT rule had a real service to block, confirmed listening via /proc/net/tcp

Verified from node2 and node3: nc to node1:23 refused (connection refused) while nc to node1:22 (ssh) succeeds, proving the rule is scoped correctly; nmap broadcast-dhcp-discover shows node1 (10.100.34.10) issuing a DHCPOFFER in the 100-249 range alongside the platform's own DHCP server
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id, uci config, dnsmasq/service status, DHCP-offer and telnet-block tests) on all three nodes

Restarted node1 via background-scheduled 'reboot' so the ack returned before disconnect; polled until exec was available again; confirmed boot_id changed (0c17c277... -> 41d9f57b...); re-verified static IP, firewall rule, dhcp.lan.force config, dnsmasq running, DHCP offers reaching node2/node3, and TCP 23 still refused post-reboot
Restarted node2 (sudo -n reboot); confirmed boot_id changed (cfdbaef8... -> 2316fd5e...); re-verified IP, connectivity to node1, DHCP offer from node1, and telnet block post-reboot
Restarted node3 (sudo -n reboot); confirmed boot_id changed (8d1d94e2... -> 9590eef3...); re-verified IP, connectivity to node1, DHCP offer from node1, and telnet block post-reboot
Final health re-check on node1 after all three node restarts completed, confirming config and dnsmasq service remained intact

evidence.requirement: node1 has a fixed static address of its own on the shared network
evidence.summary: network.lan proto changed to static with ipaddr=10.100.34.10; confirmed applied both immediately after change and again after node1's reboot

evidence.requirement: node1 provides DHCP service for node2 and node3
evidence.summary: dnsmasq initially refused to start due to detecting the platform DHCP server; force=1 fix applied and dnsmasq bound to udp/67; nmap broadcast-dhcp-discover from node2 and node3 both show node1 (10.100.34.10) responding with a DHCPOFFER

evidence.requirement: firewall rule refusing TCP port 23 from the private network
evidence.summary: Block-Telnet-From-LAN rule added (src=lan, tcp, dest_port=23, REJECT); socat listener placed on port 23; nc from node2 and node3 to node1:23 refused while node1:22 succeeds

evidence.requirement: node1 restart persistence: boot identity change and recovered config/services/traffic
evidence.summary: Pre-reboot boot_id captured, reboot acknowledged and returned, node unreachable then back up with new boot_id (0c17c277...->41d9f57b...); static IP/firewall/dhcp config confirmed intact; DHCP offers and telnet-block re-verified live from node2/node3 post-reboot

evidence.requirement: node2 restart persistence: boot identity change and recovered network/data-plane health
evidence.summary: sudo reboot acknowledged, node back up with new boot_id (cfdbaef8...->2316fd5e...); IP restored, ping to node1 succeeds, telnet still refused, DHCP offer from node1 still received

evidence.requirement: node3 restart persistence: boot identity change and recovered network/data-plane health
evidence.summary: sudo reboot acknowledged, node back up with new boot_id (8d1d94e2...->9590eef3...); IP restored, ping to node1 succeeds, telnet still refused, DHCP offer from node1 still received

evidence.requirement: node1 remains healthy after all three sequential node restarts completed
evidence.summary: Final check confirms node1's boot_id, static IP config, firewall rule, and running dnsmasq service are all still intact after node2 and node3 were also restarted
